fieldMarks: Rufous or grayish-brown above with a blackish stripe down the back; whitish belly and inner legs.
Long hair on the throat, chest and front legs; no beard.
Horns curve outward, backward and then inward, with transverse wrinkles; yellowish-brown, darkening with age.
Females are much smaller (to about 65 kg) with smaller horns; males reach about 145 kg.
behavior: Lives in small mixed-sex groups and climbs steep slopes expertly.
Eats browse, grasses and forbs (one study: 49% browse, 42% grass, 9% forbs) and can survive without free water.
Breeding peaks mid-September to mid-November; lambs born late February through April.
habitat: Dry, rough, barren and largely waterless rocky terrain, similar to desert bighorn sheep country.
range: Native to North Africa. Introduced to New Mexico (1950) and Texas (Palo Duro Canyon, 1957–1958) and now established in the Texas Panhandle canyons, Trans-Pecos and Edwards Plateau.

lookalikes.name: Bighorn sheep
lookalikes.howToTell: Aoudad have long hair on the throat, chest and forelegs; they share similar terrain and may compete with bighorns.
